name: bind_re_match_
title: Match a data frame column and attach the results

origin.description: The same attachment as bind_re_match. R's quoting of from is unnecessary in Python, so both take the column name as a string.
origin.details: The same attachment as bind_re_match. R's quoting of from is unnecessary in Python, so both take the column name as a string.
origin.value: bind_re_match_ of Mazda RX4 with keep_match TRUE returns the .match value Mazda RX4.
origin.example:
cars <- data.frame(rowname = "Mazda RX4", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bind_re_match_(cars, "rowname", "^(?<make>\\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$", keep_match = TRUE)$.match

translation.description: The same attachment as bind_re_match. R's quoting of from is unnecessary in Python, so both take the column name as a string.
translation.details: The same attachment as bind_re_match. R's quoting of from is unnecessary in Python, so both take the column name as a string.
translation.value: bind_re_match_ of Mazda RX4 with keep_match True returns the .match value Mazda RX4.
translation.example:
from rematch2 import bind_re_match_
from tibble import tibble
cars = tibble(rowname=["Mazda RX4"])
print(bind_re_match_(cars, "rowname", r"^(?<make>\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$", keep_match=True)[".match"])
